question: Should OpenClaw accept `SourceActor` and the `SourceActor*` scalar mirrors as the generic channel attribution contract in the plugin SDK now, and land this stack after the Signal mention prerequisites?
rationale: The code path is clean and tested, but the change creates a new public plugin/context contract and the permanent API shape is a maintainer product decision, not a mechanical repair.

options.title: Accept contract in stack order
options.body: Land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96738 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96862 first, then rebase and merge this PR as the canonical source-actor channel contract.

options.title: Narrow before merge
options.body: Ask the author to reduce or rename the SDK/prompt fields before merge if maintainers want a smaller attribution surface.

options.title: Defer API direction
options.body: Pause or close this PR if source-actor attribution should wait for the memory/storage attribution design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96864.

recommendation.title: Accept contract in stack order
recommendation.body: Land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96738 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96862 first, then rebase and merge this PR as the canonical source-actor channel contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for Signal runtime, plugin SDK surface, and inbound mention policy is Peter Steinberger's prior work on those seams.
